subject: Site7 on-prem Kubernetes: local-zone affinity, PV placement, DNS & NTP notes
messages:
From: James Smith <j.smith@site7-inc.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Site7 preflight questions: local-zone affinity & PVs

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of items we need to lock down before the rack install:

1) Local-zone affinity: we plan to have two racks (rack-a/rack-b) in the same colo room; we'd like to avoid cross-rack PV mounts for performance reasons. Can Redwood support nodeSelectors/affinity to keep pods + PVs co-located?

2) PV visibility: our ops team wants clear guidance on PVC binding behavior across multiple storage classes (fast-ssd, bulk-slow). We need a mapping that ties tenant classes to physical pools.

3) DNS & NTP: the colo provides an internal DNS and NTP service. Are there recommendations for kube-proxy/dnsCache or host NTP sync that you require?

We have an on-site tech week starting Nov 22 — would like to sign off on a deployment plan by Nov 16.

Attachments: inventory.csv (sent separately by procurement)

Regards,
James
Operations Lead, Site7 Inc.
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: James Smith <j.smith@site7-inc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T14:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Site7 preflight questions: local-zone affinity & PVs

James — thanks, good questions. High level answers and a proposed checklist below; attaching a simple node-affinity diagram and PV-class mapping for your storage team.

Summary answers (short):
- Yes — we will implement nodeAffinity + pod anti/soft-affinity to keep workloads in-rack. We'll also mark fast-ssd PVs with a topology key so PVCs bind only to same-rack volumes.
- PV mapping: see attached spreadsheet. We'll create StorageClasses: redwood-fast-ssd (volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer, topologyKeys: topology.kubernetes.io/rack), redwood-bulk (Immediate/Wait depending on pool).
- DNS & NTP: prefer enabling host NTP sync and using the colo NTP IPs. For DNS, we recommend CoreDNS config with forwarders to the colo resolver and enable stubDomain for internal zones. Run kube-dns cache TTL tuning to reduce external lookups.

Proposed short checklist (for sign-off):
- [ ] Confirm rack topology labels on node inventory (rack=a|b) — ops to provide mapping by Nov 12
- [ ] Approve PV class mappings in attached pv-class-mapping.xlsx
- [ ] Approve enabling topology.kubernetes.io/rack key for PVs
- [ ] Confirm NTP IPs and whether host-level NTP is enforced by colo
- [ ] Window for control-plane bring-up (suggest Nov 23 morning)

Notes/technical detail (for Karthik/Marissa):
- We'll use WaitForFirstConsumer on redwood-fast-ssd so the scheduler picks a node in the desired rack and the dynamic provisioner creates a volume in the same topo. Must ensure CSI driver supports topology. If local PV driver is used, we'll pre-provision hostPath-backed volumes per node with matching labels.
- For cross-rack fallback (rare): we can configure a policy that allows binding to bulk pool in other rack with a higher latency class; we'll only enable on explicit acceptance.

Attachments: site7-node-affinity-diagram.svg, pv-class-mapping.xlsx, ntp-dns-checklist.md

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, James Smith <j.smith@site7-inc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Site7 preflight questions: local-zone affinity & PVs

Adding a few implementation details from the storage side:

- StorageClasses: We'll propose 3 classes in the spreadsheet: redwood-fast-ssd, redwood-standard-ssd, redwood-bulk-hdd. Recommended volumeBindingMode:
  * fast-ssd: WaitForFirstConsumer (enforces rack locality)
  * standard-ssd: WaitForFirstConsumer
  * bulk-hdd: Immediate (pre-provisioned pool, cross-rack ok if capacity concerns)

- CSI driver: confirm with colo whether their block provider exposes topology keys (we can work with them to add topology.kubernetes.io/rack). If topology isn't exposed, we'll fallback to nodeAffinity + pre-provisioned local PVs (node-level labels) and the storage operator will prefer same-node volumes.

- PV eviction/DR: recommend a retention policy: keep replicas for 24h and delayed deletion for 2h after node drain. We'll include a short runbook item to avoid accidental cross-rack deletes during maintenance.

Minor ask to Site7: please include service endpoints for internal DNS and the NTP servers in your next reply so we can bake them into the manifests.

Marissa
Principal Storage Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: James Smith <j.smith@site7-inc.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T15:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Site7 preflight questions: local-zone affinity & PVs

James — thanks for the quick turn. Confirming next steps and dates so we can sign off before your tech week: 

1) Ops to provide node->rack mapping + DNS/NTP endpoints by EOD Nov 12 (you'd previously mentioned Nov 12, please confirm).
2) Redwood to produce final manifests and a brief preflight checklist by Nov 14. We'll include:
   - Node labels and nodeAffinity examples
   - StorageClass YAMLs for redwood-fast-ssd / redwood-standard-ssd / redwood-bulk-hdd
   - CoreDNS forward/stubDomain snippets and kubelet NTP host config recommendations
   - Rollback plan for PV fallback (cross-rack bind consent flow)
3) Control-plane bring-up tentatively Nov 23 morning; we'll keep a 2-hour window for initial smoke tests and metric checks.

If Site7 confirms the inventory mapping and NTP/DNS IPs today we can hit Nov 14 for manifests. If not, we'll need to push the preflight to Nov 18.

Thanks — looping Karthik for any infra-specific constraints on our side (e.g., quantization of topology keys).

Irene Choi
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
